than shipping two denominations\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022## Background\\n\\nTwo related findings from operating the platform, diagnosed live on 2026-08-30.\\n\\nFirst, the node ceiling is denominated in agent sessions (maxConcurrentAgentSessions), but a run reserves its peak of 2 sessions at admission for its whole life, so the setting has dead values: 3 admits exactly what 2 admits (one run). The operator who designed the system set 3 expecting three units of concurrency and got one.\\n\\nSecond, the slot reservation is bookkeeping, not live agents: a run spawns 1 agent during build, 2 only during the two-lens review passes, 1 during fix and verify sessions, and 0 during verification gates. The whole-life reservation exists only to make admission arithmetic safe.\\n\\n## Design rulings (Brian, 2026-08-30)\\n\\n1. **The node setting is task runs, named max-concurrent-task-runs.** How many task executions are live is the thing the operator actually reasons about; session arithmetic moves inside the daemon. Naming ruling (Brian, 2026-08-30): the compound \\u0022task runs\\u0022 was chosen over bare \\u0022runs\\u0022 (does not say what runs) and over \\u0022max-tasks-in-flight\\u0022 (reads well but \\u0022in flight\\u0022 appears nowhere else in the platform\\u0027s vocabulary, while \\u0022run\\u0022 is the domain\\u0027s first-class term for one execution of one task); the project-level ceiling uses the same words so the term is learned once.\\n2. **A second knob caps sessions within one run.** Global default 3, hardcoded as the default value of a durable global setting; a per-task CLI override can raise or lower it ad hoc, even mid-run. With the two knobs, runs=1 plus cap=1 is a strict-serial maximum-throttle mode, and the total possible live sessions on a node is runs x cap, emergent rather than configured.\\n3. **Cap 1 means serialized lenses.** The two-lens phases dispatch one lens at a time. This throttles burn RATE, not total tokens - the same reviews run, spread over more wall clock - and the task records that distinction so nobody mistakes it for a savings lever.\\n4. **Default 3 is deliberate headroom.** Nothing today spawns a third concurrent session within a run; the room is for future machinery (for example a quick side-session dispatched alongside a fix session - discussed, explicitly not in scope here).\\n5. **Reservation dissolves.** With admission counting runs, the whole-life 2-session reservation is no longer needed as a concept; phases spawn what they need up to the run\\u0027s cap.\\n6. **Concurrency within a run is bounded by coded capability, not agent request.** The daemon only ever spawns sessions for activities it has coded logic for, and agents never ask the daemon for a generic sibling session - they signal a waypoint through the CLI (\\u0022this activity is ready to start\\u0022) and the daemon decides dispatch, the same compose/execute discipline the Jira write surface uses. The per-run cap is therefore the ceiling on simultaneous coded activities for one task: today the daemon knows exactly two that can overlap (the review lenses), so effective concurrency is 2 by construction, and each unit above 2 becomes reachable only when a new overlappable activity is coded into the daemon with its own dispatch logic, stream events, and prompt surface. Free-form helper work inside a slot is already covered by the agent\\u0027s own in-process sub-agents, which the daemon neither sees nor governs.\\n\\n## Implementation notes\\n\\n- The dispatch log already reasons in runs (\\u0022at most N resident agent session(s), which is M live run(s) at 2 session(s) each\\u0022) - this promotes the derived M to the configured value.\\n- Config precedence (backlog 59): env var outranks config file outranks built-in default;
